releases.name: v0.14.5 — Reviewer test organization and unborn Docker proof
releases.body:
# v0.14.5 — Reviewer test organization and unborn Git proof

- Organize Reviewer correction coverage by lifecycle/self-recheck, continuation, scope, validation and permissions (#295). Retain all 209 original cases and all 81 byte-identical registration blocks; add one fixture-isolation regression. Share only plain committed Git inputs, not Mission state, native history, ledgers or plugin instances.
- Serial local observation: 209 cases in 107.027 s before; 210 cases in 101.358 s after (5.669 s / 5.3% lower). This is one before/after observation, not a statistical or full-suite speed claim. The main benefit is focused execution and smaller, purpose-specific files; no test deletion or production cache.
- Observe fresh Git-only Docker workspaces before their first commit (#294). Only an absent symbolic HEAD target permits the repository-format empty-tree comparison. Existing/broken refs and failed observations remain unavailable. No initial commit, Git identity, task dependency installation or object write is required.

## Review and retained work

Collected PR bodies, ordinary comments, review bodies and inline comments before integration, and retained later feedback before publication. PRs #294–#296 returned no concrete external code finding; all three eventually reported automated review unavailable because of usage limits. PR #295 initially returned no existing review body, inline finding or ordinary comment at integration. CI success, failed summary flags without concrete findings, and unavailable review are not independent PASS.

The current all-PR release instruction authorizes integrating the retained, previously paused #294 change. It does not resume the prior benchmark campaign, replay trials/grades, alter holds or increase its budget. Existing findings, measured spend and unknown usage remain retained.

## Release verification

Fix the integrated `main` commit and one tarball before candidate preflight and `npm run test:full`. Check fixed-commit Windows CI and real native Worker startup/model identity. Use the same tarball for both npm global prefixes, the OpenCode config-local package, GitHub Release and npm publication. Command/exit/timing receipts, original and final test logs, review dispositions, hashes and inference costs remain under `_testenv/releases/0.14.5/`.

Mission marker: `0.14.5-unborn-proof-v1`. Codex skill marker: `0.13.11-codex-skill-v2`. Restart OpenCode after global apply and verify the loaded runtime. Worker startup is distinct from Mission completion and official scoring.

releases.name: v0.14.4 — Docker candidate reads and Worker dispatch
releases.body:
# v0.14.4 — Docker candidate reads and Worker dispatch

- Accept a different Worker display description when the exact Task reference, agent, owner and continuation identity still match. The child receives the retained canonical Task; special repair dispatch keeps exact matching (#289).
- Preserve declared Docker CWD aliases while binding their physical execution directory; retain discovered Git roots without HEAD and preserve actual root-path whitespace (#282, #287).
- Bind Git-only candidate proof to actual file bytes and metadata, including ignored inputs, executable modes, symlink referents and working bytes hidden by Git index flags. Observation failures cannot yield partial proof (#283, #284, #288, #292).
- Inspect the regular-file referents already captured through candidate-local links. Preserve entry association and the existing captured-input footprint (#290).
- Keep native read pages valid after JSON escaping and stream long logical lines with bounded excerpts and whole-file hashes. Git-only images use a fixed read transport when task Python is absent (#285, #286, #291).

## Review and retained work

PR bodies, ordinary comments, review bodies and inline comments for #282–#292 were collected. Automated Codex review was unavailable because of usage limits; no concrete external review body or inline finding was returned. Recorded same-PR self-review corrections and their final related checks remain retained. CI success and unavailable external review are not independent PASS.

The current all-PR release instruction authorizes #289 integration. Its [paused v0.14.3 campaign](frontier-clean30-v0143-20261017.md) remains historical: nine tasks started, six graded with two correct, three ungraded, zero completed Missions. Original findings, the consumed 38-unit Mission budget, unknown usage and holds remain intact. This release does not resume that campaign or claim an independent final Mission PASS.

releases.body:
# v0.14.3 — workspace proof and reliable continuation

- Bind native Docker validation to the actual task container, CWD and candidate bytes, including non-Git/ignored inputs. Connect native proof to Worker settlement and independent Reviewer inspection. Resolve both retained #280 Medium findings: generated gateway correction permissions and isolated Python reads (#279, #280).
- Preserve successful, still-fresh validation prefixes when retrying a failed tail; recover completed validation history across compaction (#275, #279).
- Retain owned-server termination diagnostics, distinguish zombies from surviving process groups, retire previous watchdogs on recovery, and bind CLI settlement to its owned native root (#271, #272, #278).
- Keep actionable status, observed models and failure facts visible under native output truncation. Preserve native model usage, including completed compaction, and select the correct Mission/Worker lineage (#273, #276, #277).
- Recover Frontier artifacts after agent failures and expose reusable native gateway preparation. Historical campaigns, results, findings and unknown usage remain retained (#274, #280).

Existing PR bodies, ordinary comments, review bodies and inline comments for #271–#280 were collected. Concrete findings were fixed with related regressions; #279/#280 automated review usage limits remain recorded as unavailable review. releases.name: v0.14.2 — Exact cold resume and owned-server exit
releases.body:
# v0.14.2 — exact cold resume and owned-server exit

- Restore a retained Codex Coordinator when its parent Task item is missing, accept explicit failed receipts in completed parent turns, and return the same Task instead of waiting on an ended dispatch. CLI progress shows the restored Mission, Coordinator and next action (#268).
- Resolve both #268 P1 findings: recover nested Worker receipts before replacing the predecessor owner generation, and persist/verify the current Coordinator dispatch-to-native-message binding. Earlier terminal turns cannot settle a newer missing turn; existing terminal parent receipts retain their normal reconciliation path.
- End CLI probe settlement waiting when its owned server exits. Preserve the original CLI exit, server failure, first stop cause and unresolved usage reservation; intentional teardown is not reported as server loss (#269).
- Retain the [Codex Anko recovery record](benchmarks/codex-coordinator-cold-resume-20261016.md) and [interrupted Frontier run record](frontier-clean30-20261016-recovery.md). Their fixed runtimes, original results and limits remain historical measurements, not a new v0.14.2 benchmark score.
